guide.title: This is the story of scaling operations from "running" to "optimizing", not just adding more servers.
guide.problem: As the number of orders, warehouses, products and partners increases, paper-based picking, approximate inventory management, file exchange and manual accounting processing are no longer fast or accurate enough. Each step of delivery opens up a series of after-sales and financial problems behind.
guide.core_idea: Operation Product progressively digitizes the entire lifecycle: precise inventory location, pick-by-batch and optimal routing, warehouse PDA, delivery route configuration, partner integration, proof-of-delivery, after-sales and receivable/payable flows.
guide.outcome: Once the basic foundation is up and running, the next focus turns to inventory optimization, single prioritization, real-time routing, accounting automation and human capacity building. The article puts process and organizational quality on an equal footing with algorithms.
takeaways: A local optimization is only valid when the input data is sufficiently accurate; Good picking paths don't help if the system doesn't know which shelf the product is actually on.
Designing for the operator needs to reduce cognitive load and make exceptions clear, because physical deviations often start with manual operations.
Logistics integration is a long state machine: handover, shipping, collection, status updates and proof of delivery all need to be controlled.
The financial system is subject to a different type of scale: it is not necessarily the lowest latency, but the data must be traceable and accurate for each transaction.
The next stage of scaling is often about optimizing decisions and people, not just replacing new technology.
review_lenses: Draw the state machine from inbound to aftermarket and show the owner of each transition.
Design a reconcile mechanism when other system data exists in physical inventory or partner data.
Set end-to-end metrics like delivery time, cost per order, and defect rate instead of just service-specific metrics.
Evaluate the UX of internal tools by operational errors, training time, and actual operator productivity.
